steps.title: Get one row per category
steps.change: Each input row is a product and each output row is a category. All the fields come from Products, so this query reads a single table.
steps.added_sql:
SELECT CategoryID, COUNT(ProductID) AS products
FROM Products
GROUP BY CategoryID
ORDER BY CategoryID;

steps.title: Add the sale-price statistics
steps.change: Category 10 has sale prices of 80 and 100. The minimum is 80, the maximum is 100, and the mean is 90.
steps.added_sql:
SELECT CategoryID, COUNT(ProductID) AS products,
       MIN(Sale_Price) AS min_price,
       MAX(Sale_Price) AS max_price,
       ROUND(AVG(Sale_Price), 2) AS avg_price
steps.sql:
SELECT CategoryID, COUNT(ProductID) AS products,
       MIN(Sale_Price) AS min_price,
       MAX(Sale_Price) AS max_price,
       ROUND(AVG(Sale_Price), 2) AS avg_price
FROM Products
GROUP BY CategoryID
ORDER BY CategoryID;

steps.title: Preview the contribution of each product
steps.change: Compare each product's own sale and market prices. Their valid discounts are 20% and 0%, so both contribute to the average.
steps.added_sql:
SELECT ProductID, CategoryID,
       CASE WHEN Sale_Price = Market_Price THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS full_price_flag,
       CASE
           WHEN Market_Price IS NOT NULL AND Market_Price != 0
           THEN (Market_Price - Sale_Price) * 100.0 / Market_Price
       END AS product_discount_pct
-- …
ORDER BY ProductID;
